title: Warm-up: queues and stacks
description: Check the ideas you'll need for traversals.

questions.prompt: A queue holds 4, 9 and 2. The 4 was added first. You remove one item. Which item comes out?
questions.explanation: A queue is first in, first out (FIFO), so 4, the first item added, leaves first.

questions.prompt: You push 4, then 9, then 2 onto a stack. You pop one item. Which item comes out?
questions.explanation: A stack is last in, first out (LIFO), so 2, the last item pushed, comes out first.

questions.prompt: Which structure is "first in, first out"?
questions.explanation: A queue is FIFO. A stack is LIFO.

questions.prompt: A function that calls itself is called…
questions.explanation: A recursive function calls itself. Each call waits on the call stack until the calls it made return.

questions.prompt: Which node is the root of this tree?
questions.explanation: The root is the single node at the top, with no parent: 50.

questions.prompt: How many leaves does this tree have?
questions.explanation: Leaves have no children: 20, 40, 60 and 80. That's 4.

questions.prompt: What is the height of this tree, counting edges?
questions.explanation: The longest path from the root to a leaf, such as 50 → 30 → 20, has 2 edges.

questions.prompt: In a binary tree, each node has…
questions.explanation: "Binary" sets a maximum of two children. A node can also have one child or none.

title: Lesson 2 practice quiz
description: The BST rule, search and insert.

questions.prompt: A BST's root holds 50. Where must the value 45 be?
questions.explanation: 45 < 50, and the BST rule puts every smaller value in the left subtree.

questions.prompt: You insert 35 into this BST. Where does it go?
questions.explanation: 35 < 50 → left; 35 > 30 → right; 35 < 40 → left. 40 has no left child, so 35 goes there.

questions.prompt: How many comparisons does it take to find 60 in this BST?
questions.explanation: 60 is compared with 50, then 70, then 60: three comparisons.

questions.prompt: You insert 10, 20, 30, 40 into an empty BST, in that order. What do you get?

options.text: A lopsided chain, so search becomes O(n)

questions.explanation: Each value is larger than the last, so every node goes to the right. The tree becomes a chain.

title: Lesson 3 practice quiz
description: BFS and the three DFS orders.

questions.prompt: Tap the nodes in the order BFS visits them.
questions.explanation: BFS finishes each level, left to right, before moving down: 50, then 30 and 70, then the bottom row.

questions.prompt: Which data structure does BFS use to decide what to visit next?
questions.explanation: A queue. Children join at the back, so a whole level is visited before the next one.

questions.prompt: Which DFS order lists a BST's values from smallest to largest?
questions.explanation: In-order visits left, node, right. In a BST that is exactly smallest to largest.

questions.prompt: What is the post-order of this tree?
questions.explanation: Post-order visits both children before the node, so the root, 50, always comes last.

title: Final check: all lessons
description: One question set across all three lessons.

questions.prompt: How many leaves does this tree have?
questions.explanation: 15, 35 and 55 have no children. 65 has one child (55), so it is not a leaf.

questions.prompt: You insert 58 into this BST. Where does it go?
questions.explanation: 58 > 45 → right; 58 < 65 → left; 58 > 55 → right. 55 has no right child, so 58 goes there.

questions.prompt: Tap the nodes in the order BFS visits them.
questions.explanation: Level by level: 45, then 25 and 65, then 15, 35 and 55.

questions.prompt: What is the pre-order of this tree?
questions.explanation: Pre-order visits the node first, then its left subtree, then its right: 45, 25, 15, 35, 65, 55.

questions.prompt: Tap the nodes in in-order (left, node, right).
questions.explanation: In-order of a BST gives the values sorted from smallest to largest.

questions.prompt: Why can searching a BST become as slow as searching a list?

options.text: Sorted inserts make a lopsided chain

questions.explanation: If values arrive in sorted order, every node goes to one side and search takes O(n).
